page: Amazon Web Services i7ie.metal-24xl is a bare-metal, storage-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8559C processor providing 48 physical cores and 96 vCPUs operating at a base frequency of 3.2 GHz. The hardware architecture incorporates 320 MB of L3 cache alongside support for advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), and hardware-accelerated cryptography. System memory comprises 768.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 RAM configured at 8.0 GB per vCPU. Network throughput is provisioned at a baseline of 100 Gbps, and the bare-metal profile includes no hypervisor layer.

Storage capabilities represent the primary differentiator of this instance, which packages 60,000 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity directly on the host. This massive internal storage array is paired with substantial memory throughput, registering uncached read bandwidth of 289.33 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 119.86 GB/sec in benchmark testing. Compute performance demonstrates high throughput across multi-core workloads, supported by a PassMark CPU score of 95,190.03, a Geekbench multi-core score of 22,291.0, and strong performance in multi-threaded decompression tests yielding 547.89 GB/sec.

Hardware-level vector extensions (AMX and AVX-512) directly boost specialized computational profiles, showing top-tier performance in database operations (PassMark score of 33,739.36) and large-model prompt processing reaching 39.16 tokens/sec. The configuration lacks discrete GPU hardware, which shifts all machine learning inference and parallel tasks exclusively to the host CPU cores. While multi-threaded execution and I/O remain in upper tiers, single-threaded throughput falls in the average bracket, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2,160.09.

From an infrastructure perspective, the server maximizes density by co-locating massive NVMe capacity, large DDR5 memory footprints, and bare-metal access on a single host. It eliminates the virtualization overhead typically associated with multi-tenant storage nodes. AWS i7ie.metal-24xl is designed for high-capacity operational databases, distributed transactional datastores, low-latency caching arrays, large-scale data ingestion pipelines, and search engine indices requiring extensive local persistence.
description: Amazon Web Services i7ie.metal-24xl is a bare-metal storage-optimized server powered by a 48-core, 96-thread Intel Xeon 8559C processor running at 3.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system integrates 768.0 GB of high-frequency DDR5 memory and 60,000 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage, supported by 100 Gbps baseline networking and zero hypervisor overhead. Benchmark evaluations reflect top-tier multi-threaded and database performance, including 33,739.36 on PassMark database tests, a PassMark CPU score of 95,190.03, and 117.71 million Redis SET operations per second. While the instance does not feature dedicated GPUs and exhibits mid-range single-core compute performance, its massive local I/O capacity and AMX/AVX-512 instruction sets deliver high efficiency for resource-dense setups. This profile fits high-throughput distributed databases, low-latency operational data stores, search indexing, and real-time transaction processing workloads.
